name: Adaptive Biotechnologies Corporation

profile.description: Adaptive Biotechnologies develops an immune medicine platform combining proprietary chemistry, computational biology, and machine learning to decode the adaptive immune system. Its primary commercial product, clonoSEQ, is the first and only FDA-cleared assay for Minimal Residual Disease (MRD) detection in blood cancers. The company also operates life sciences research and drug discovery businesses, leveraging its immunosequencing platform and partnerships with Microsoft and Genentech.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Innovation Track Record (2/3): Adaptive achieved 55% full-year 2025 revenue growth to $277M, driven by clonoSEQ MRD adoption that grew 46% YoY to 105,600 tests, and Q1 2026 continued with 53% MRD revenue growth and 41% volume increase to 32,595 tests [1][2]. The company successfully brought MRD testing from research concept to clinical standard of care. AI Deployment (2/2): The Microsoft partnership applies machine learning and cloud computing to decode the adaptive immune system, creating a universal blood test platform for disease detection [3]. AI/ML is embedded in the core immunosequencing platform — this is genuinely AI-native diagnostics where computational biology drives every clinical result. Market Share (2/2): clonoSEQ is the only FDA-cleared MRD test in the United States, giving Adaptive a category-defining monopoly with 100% share of the FDA-cleared MRD space. Test volume of 105,600 (+39% YoY) demonstrates accelerating clinical adoption [1]. Product Pipeline (1/2): FY2026 MRD revenue guidance of $260-270M provides clear visibility, with expansion into additional cancer indications underway. The Microsoft partnership for universal immune-based disease detection remains in development without specific launch dates [2]. R&D Intensity (1/1): As a platform biotech with 74.6% gross margins reinvesting heavily in R&D, Adaptive's spending intensity exceeds most diagnostic peers.

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): CEO Chad Robins articulates a specific, purpose-driven mission to 'translate the genetics of the adaptive immune system into clinical products to diagnose and treat disease' — this is distinctive, connects the company's work to transforming medicine, and differentiates Adaptive from generic biotech companies [3]. The mission clearly reflects genuine intentionality and deep thought. Community Impact (1/2): Adaptive has Employee Resource Groups and sustainability initiatives, and its products serve patients with blood cancers in clinical settings where MRD testing improves treatment decisions — providing genuine medical value [1]. Employee Retention (0/2): Glassdoor rating of 3.3/5 with 234 reviews is below average. Reviews cite 'constant layoffs and no loyalty to those who put in years of hard work,' and the Executive Team is rated in the bottom 40% on Comparably, indicating significant trust and retention challenges [4]. Insider Buying (0/2): CEO Robins is a co-founder with significant equity ownership, but no evidence of meaningful recent open-market insider purchases was found.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as Growth stock. Adaptive's revenue growth profile is exceptional — 55% YoY and 35.8% 5yr CAGR to $277M — driving perfect scores on growth metrics [1][5]. D/E of 93% is manageable with $218M cash against $208M debt, scoring 0.90 [5]. PEG of 0.6 reflects the market's expectation of rapid earnings improvement as the company approaches profitability, scoring perfectly [5]. However, ROE of -27.8% and profit margin of -21.5% score 0.0, reflecting continued unprofitability despite 74.6% gross margins and a narrowing loss (EPS improved from -$1.08 to -$0.39 in FY2025) [1][5]. Forward P/E excluded as company remains GAAP-unprofitable. Management projects positive adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow by end of 2026 [1]. Liquidity floor easily cleared: 2.55M avg vol x $22.29 = $56.9M [5].

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): Adaptive's clonoSEQ diagnostic requires proprietary wet-lab chemistry, biological sample processing, and FDA clearance — creating a regulatory and physical infrastructure moat that AI alone cannot replicate [1]. The immunosequencing platform generates proprietary data from physical patient samples, building a defensible data moat that grows with each test performed. Clinical validation requirements and FDA regulatory pathways take years, protecting the incumbent position. AI could enable competitors to develop alternative MRD detection approaches, but the regulatory timeline and clinical evidence requirements provide durable protection. AI Opportunity (1/1): AI is foundational to Adaptive's business — the Microsoft partnership uses machine learning to decode immune system patterns for disease detection, and the entire immunosequencing platform relies on computational biology and ML for clinical interpretation [3]. The company is both protected by and powered by AI.

infinite_game.summary: Adaptive demonstrates genuine purpose-driven leadership under co-founder CEO Chad Robins, with a 17-year commitment to decoding the adaptive immune system. The Just Cause is distinctive and partially validated by commercial execution ($277M revenue). However, Glassdoor's 3.3/5 rating with reports of 'constant layoffs' and Executive Team in the bottom 40% on Comparably indicate significant organizational trust deficits that undermine the infinite game thesis [3][4].

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Translating the genetics of the adaptive immune system into clinical products represents a genuine Just Cause — it envisions a future where the immune system becomes a diagnostic window into health and disease that doesn't exist today [3]. Robins co-founded the company in 2009 around this vision and has led it through 17 years of platform development into a $277M commercial business. The cause is distinctive, service-oriented, and big enough to never be fully achieved. However, it hasn't yet been tested through a major crisis or leadership transition.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Despite CEO Robins' stated emphasis on culture-building, employee data tells a different story. Glassdoor rating of 3.3/5 with 234 reviews is below industry average. Reviews cite 'constant layoffs and no loyalty to those who put in years of hard work,' and the Executive Team is rated in the bottom 40% on Comparably [4]. This pattern of workforce reductions alongside culture rhetoric suggests a gap between stated values and organizational reality.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No evidence of management adopting an infinite competitive mindset toward rivals. CEO Robins states he wants Adaptive to be 'compared to the disruptive, game-changing companies across the board' — an aspirational, comparative framing rather than the humble acknowledgment of competitors' strengths that Sinek would look for [3]. Partnerships with Microsoft and Genentech reflect strategic necessity, not competitive learning.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Adaptive has evolved from a research-stage immunosequencing company to a commercial diagnostics business, pivoting from pure research tools to an FDA-cleared clinical product in clonoSEQ [1]. The expansion from MRD testing into broader immune medicine applications shows strategic evolution. However, the company has not yet faced a true existential pivot decision that required abandoning a profitable business line.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Robins invested 17 years building the immunosequencing platform before reaching significant commercial scale, forgoing near-term profits for long-term platform value [3]. The decision to pursue FDA clearance for clonoSEQ — a costly and uncertain regulatory path — showed willingness to choose the harder path for durable competitive advantage. The company continues to invest heavily in R&D despite persistent losses.

investment_thesis: Adaptive Biotechnologies holds a monopoly position in FDA-cleared MRD testing with clonoSEQ, the only approved assay for detecting residual cancer cells in blood cancer patients. FY2025 revenue grew 55% to $277M with 74.6% gross margins, and Q1 2026 continued the momentum with MRD revenue up 53% YoY and test volume up 41% to 32,595 [1][2]. The MRD business achieved segment profitability in mid-2025, and management projects positive adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow for the full company by end of 2026. FY2026 MRD guidance of $260-270M implies 22-27% growth from an accelerating base [2]. The Microsoft partnership for AI-powered universal immune diagnostics represents transformative optionality beyond MRD. At $22.29 with a PEG of 0.6, the valuation is reasonable for a clinical monopoly approaching profitability with 55% revenue growth and 35.8% 5yr CAGR [5].
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on persistent unprofitability and competitive risk. Despite 55% revenue growth, Adaptive still posted a -21.5% net margin with loss per share of -$0.39 in FY2025 — though significantly improved from -$1.08 in FY2024 [1][5]. Operating expenses of $350-360M for 2026 against projected ~$340M revenue leaves a narrow path to profitability. The stock has rallied 54% from $14.47 to $22.29, pricing in significant improvement that must be delivered. The Genentech partnership exit removed drug discovery revenue and validated concerns about expanding beyond diagnostics into therapeutics. The clonoSEQ monopoly could face competition from next-generation sequencing competitors or liquid biopsy companies entering MRD. Glassdoor 3.3/5 with reports of 'constant layoffs' suggests talent retention risk that could impair execution during a critical scaling phase [4]. D/E of 93% with $218M cash against $208M debt provides adequate but not expansive liquidity runway.
key_catalysts: Expected inflection to positive adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow by end of 2026, validating the commercial model and potentially triggering institutional investor re-rating [1][2]
clonoSEQ test volume growth of 30-40%+ in 2026, with FY2026 MRD guidance of $260-270M and expansion into additional cancer indications as MRD becomes standard of care [2]
Microsoft AI partnership for universal immune system-based blood test could open a massive TAM beyond oncology into autoimmune and infectious disease detection [3]
key_risks: Persistent unprofitability with -21.5% net margin despite 55% revenue growth and 74.6% gross margins — path to company-level profitability requires tight expense discipline against a narrow margin for error [1][5]
Stock has rallied 54% from $14.47, pricing in substantial profitability improvement — any miss on MRD growth or operating expense targets could trigger significant pullback [5]

Talent retention risk with Glassdoor 3.3/5, reports of 'constant layoffs,' and Executive Team rated in bottom 40% on Comparably during a critical scaling phase that requires hiring and retaining top talent [4]
